title: Bias, Confounding, and Association and Causation

steps.tx: An **association** exists when two variables occur together more often than chance predicts. Associations are either **spurious**, meaning not real, or real. Real associations are direct (one to one causal, or multifactorial) or indirect, where a third factor links both. Descriptive studies suggest hypotheses; analytic and experimental studies test them.
steps.say: An association exists when two variables occur together more often than chance would predict. Associations are either spurious, meaning not real, or real. Real associations are direct, either one to one causal or multifactorial, or indirect, where a third factor links both. Descriptive studies suggest hypotheses, while analytic and experimental studies test them.

steps.tx: Confounding is removed mainly by **matching**, which distributes known confounders equally between groups. Randomisation is the second best method and is the basis of trials. Restriction, stratification and multivariate analysis are other options. Blinding does not remove confounding; it controls observer and subject bias.

steps.tx: The neon graphic separates true causation from distortion by a third factor. Exposure and outcome connect through a direct path, but a **confounder** touches both sides and can fake or hide the link. The right half shows the remedy as **matching**, with exposed and unexposed groups balanced on age and gender around a scale. Blocking the confounding path lets the true associational path stand out. The lesson ranks matching first and **randomisation** second for removing confounding.
steps.say: Follow the triangle on the left. A confounder links to both exposure and outcome, so it can mimic a causal path that is not real. The fix on the right is matching, where each exposed person is paired with an unexposed person of same age and gender, balancing the scale. Matching distributes known confounders evenly. Randomisation is the next best method and forms the basis of trials.

vis.alt: Neon triangle links exposure outcome and confounder beside balanced groups on a scale showing matching.
vis.caption: Triangle plus scale show confounding blocked by matching Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Selection bias** arises when the study population does not represent the target population, for example **Berkson bias** in hospital-based case-control studies, or **Neyman bias** where mild or fatal cases are missed. **Information bias** includes **recall bias** in case-control studies and **interviewer bias**. Blinding reduces recall and interviewer bias.

steps.tx: The **web of causation**, proposed by McMahon and Pugh, suits chronic diseases with several interacting factors. Removing a single important link may control disease. In NCDs such as coronary heart disease, causes are multifactorial, and individual factors carry unequal weight. The **ecological fallacy** occurs when group level associations are wrongly applied to individuals.

vis.caption: Chronic disease has many interacting causes: break whichever links prevention can reach.
